profile.reading: QTS Richmond 2 (RIC2) is a data center campus in Sandston, Virginia, just east of Richmond and immediately adjacent to Richmond International Airport, developed by QTS Realty Trust (formerly Quality Technology Services, renamed following the company's 2013 IPO; this registry tracks both names as the same operator). Per QTS's own site, the campus spans approximately 85 acres and is planned to include five buildings once fully built out, with a total planned capacity of 180 megawatts of IT power upon completion; that figure describes the campus as a whole rather than any single building, and much of it was not yet in operation as of the source page, so it is not applied here as this building's own confirmed capacity. This building, DC5, sits at 6060 Technology Boulevard, one of five addressed buildings running along Technology Boulevard: 6030 (DC1), 6040 (DC2), 6050 (DC3), 6060 (DC5), and 6070 (DC6); the campus's own numbering skips DC4 entirely, a naming gap this registry notes rather than attempts to explain. RIC2 is QTS's second Richmond-area campus, distinct from the company's original Richmond 1 (RIC1) campus elsewhere in the metro, which this registry documents as a separate set of facilities. Henrico County, where Sandston sits, has become one of the mid-Atlantic's fastest-growing data center corridors in recent years, drawing hyperscale and colocation development on the strength of available land, Dominion Energy transmission capacity, and dense regional fiber routes running through the Richmond area. QTS's own campus page does not state which, if any, of the five RIC2 buildings are currently operating versus still under construction, and does not publish individual square footage, IT capacity, or year-opened figures for any single building on the campus; none of those figures is asserted here for DC5 specifically, consistent with this registry's practice of reporting only what the operator has actually confirmed at the building level.

reading.body:
The Richmond 2 campus is planned to deliver 180 MW across five buildings on 85 acres when complete, but is not yet fully operational and contributes zero megawatts to current US AI infrastructure.

This facility represents future capacity rather than present infrastructure. The data distinguishes between planned generation and actual online power supply, a critical distinction for understanding AI's current grid constraint. Richmond 2 exists in the pipeline of potential compute real estate but has not yet become a binding resource in the immediate scaling problem.

The campus design, with five separate buildings on a large footprint, suggests staged deployment rather than immediate full activation. This phasing pattern is typical for major data center campuses but means the full 180 MW benefit cannot be assumed in near-term AI compute availability forecasts.

The data corrects a prior misattribution of Richmond 1 campus information to Richmond 2, indicating the importance of tracking these facilities separately by their actual physical locations and operational status. Future readings of this facility should mark when individual buildings transition from planned to online.
